title: Concepts, iterative passes & ABCD drilldown
author: Thicthor96
selftext:
Hi,

  
Want to share this process in hopes it helps you in your game development. I am pretty unartistic, but I have been able to nail down a distinct art style, and get what I consider to be amazing results in my little autobattler/minigame game. Here's what I have learned after a few months of no-lifing it's development:

  
Asking for iterative passes is a tool, doing them yourself will help bring your vision to life. Start with an art lead, and with concepts, and have an image generation api installed - I use Gemini. Ask your coordinator to add an art director agent. Its task is to ensure artistic consistency in your game. After you have a lead established, assess your art direction. Observe your assets yourself- are you happy with how they look? If you aren't, here is how I approach it:

  
"I don't like X, I would prefer if it looked more like Y. Give me 5 concepts of what this could look like- whichever I select, I want ABCD variations of that choice. Continue to iterate until I have chosen a final concept in the thread, then perform 10 iterative passes to acheive desired concept."



Director will typically recommend one, but I always choose my favorite. After you do so many of these, you can ask the coordinator to provide iterative concepts, where you run through the selection. The initial concepts presented just keep getting better, and better! 

  
Anyways hopes this helps, feel free to drop questions here
